title: Wrong milk, send it back
genre: everyday spoken American English, a short conflict at the counter
setting: the same neighborhood coffee shop, afternoon rush
mood: polite but frustrated, then quickly resolved
bed: Throughout: denser café chatter than the morning, milk steamer screaming in bursts, a grinder kicking on between lines. Dialogue stays intelligible over the noise.

speakers.name: Maya
speakers.voice: young woman, American, clear and direct, holding back irritation, medium-fast

speakers.name: Barista
speakers.voice: young man, American, slightly flustered, apologetic, medium pace

beats.text: A ceramic cup is set down on the wooden pickup counter.

beats.speaker: Maya
beats.text: Wait — this isn't oat milk. This is regular.
A beat. The steamer hisses hard, then cuts off.

beats.speaker: Barista
beats.text: Oh no. I'm really sorry — we must've grabbed the whole milk pitcher. I can remake it right now.

beats.speaker: Maya
beats.text: Yeah, please do. I'm actually dairy-free. I can't drink this.
He dumps the drink, pulls the oat carton, and the steamer starts again, shorter this time.

beats.speaker: Barista
beats.text: Totally my fault. New cup, extra shot on the house. Two minutes.

closing: The corrected cup lands on the counter with a light knock; the rush noise swallows the rest.
question: Why does Maya send the drink back?

options.label: It was made with regular milk instead of oat milk
It was too cold and she wanted it reheated
They gave her a cappuccino instead of a latte
The extra shot was missing from the order
